newsitem.title: USA: Edison Bros to file disclosure statement.
newsitem.headline: Edison Bros to file disclosure statement.

text.p: Edison Brothers Stores Inc, which filed a plan of reorganization with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del., on February 27, said Monday it expects to file its proposed disclosure statement with the court by March 31.
The retailer said it then will move for confirmation of the plan by the bankruptcy court, which could occur by mid-summer of 1997.
The plan would cancel all of Edison's existing common stock and issue 10 million shares of new common.
It also provides creditors with a combination of cash, new corporate debt and other assets to settle about $440 million in creditor claims.
Edison Brothers said its plan as filed proposes that the company's shareholders would receive two sets of warrants entitling them to buy up to nine percent of the new common stock.
The first set of warrants, which would have a three-year term, would entitle shareholders to buy four percent of the new stock at a strike price of $13.85 per share.

The second set of warrants, which would have a six-year term, would entitle holders to buy five percent of the new common stock at a strike price of $22.10 per share. The warrants would be issued at the time of the company's emergence from Chapter 11.
